column1: #The mod's own windows for OpenHOI3 (script/openhoi/windows). Read by OpenHOI3 alone: the original does not open this folder.

column2: We hold $ENERGY$ energy, $CRUDE$ crude oil and $FUEL$ fuel.
Off: the game decides - it converts only while we hold more than twice as much energy as crude oil. On: the values below decide, within what our IC allows.
Energy to spend each day. More than our IC allows is cut to it.
Never take energy below this. What industry needs today is never converted whatever this says.
Convert only while we hold less crude oil than this. 0: no limit.
No energy can be turned into crude oil yet: technology puts the rate at $RATE$, and nothing converts at 0 or below.
Developing a synthetic industry opens it. What is set above applies from then.
Today: at most $CAP$ energy a day, each making $RATE$ crude oil. $FLOOR$ energy is kept for industry.
Off: the game decides - it refines until we hold more than a year of the crude oil coming in and more than twice our crude oil. On: the values below decide, within what our IC allows.
Crude oil to refine each day. More than our IC allows is cut to it.
Never take crude oil below this.
Refine only while we hold less fuel than this. 0: no limit. The game stops at 99,000 whatever this says.
Today: at most $CAP$ crude oil a day. How much fuel it makes is the game's: technology and laws.
All amounts are a day's, in stockpile units. Type the numbers and press Apply. A country nobody plays converts as the game decides.
The utility's data is not loaded: G_ImguiUtilityEnabled is off in script/utility_settings.lua.
Not researched. Showing level 1 for reference - it is not included in the stats above.
Copy the model string to the clipboard
Waiting for the game to apply this
Drag to choose, and let go to apply. Ctrl+click the slider to type a number instead. Investment converts base IC into IC days at the shown daily rate.
Whether the decision for setting a puppet's focus is offered in game. Turning it off hides the decision.
Select a puppet to set its focus.
No country has spare production of this resource.
A trade decision can be unavailable even when a country has resources spare: each trade applies a two day cooldown that blocks the buy decision while it is handled. Wait and watch your decisions.

The focus can be changed at any time, but the effects are not instant: a new focus takes about 90 days before it gives anything, and the old one wears off over as long as it was active for. Bonuses come in three tiers, reached after 90, 360 and 720 days.
Progress towards the next building each of your ministers will place. The counters are maintained by the AI, so nothing on this page can be set.
Reads the settings back from the game, discarding edits
Never configured - showing defaults. Apply to adopt them.
Applied, with values corrected to fit the limits
Edited - press Apply to send it to the game
The largest daily money deficit the AI may run to pay for its purchases

Daily surplus is how much of a resource the AI keeps coming in each day beyond what the country actually needs. It only sells once the stockpile is above "Sell above", and cancels its own purchases once the stockpile is above "Stockpile". Supplies are left to the AI's own judgement.
Another category already uses this priority

This only takes effect with "Prioritize Upgrades/Custom" selected in the production window. IC is handed out in priority order, starting at 1, and each priority may only be used once. A category that cannot be paid for in full takes whatever is left and the ones after it get nothing. Anything still unspent goes to production. Amount is read either as a share of what the category needs or as a flat IC figure, depending on its mode.

Upgrades and reinforcement can be capped so an emergency cannot swallow the whole budget. Supply can be given a stockpile goal, which it puts a little extra IC towards until it is reached. Consumer goods can take 50% more IC while there is dissent.
The engine will not take more than $N$
Keeps producing officers for 10 more days, for a buffer of around 500

This only takes effect with "Slider AI" selected in the technology window. The numbers are resource amounts rather than slider positions: once a resource falls below its lower threshold the AI produces it until the upper threshold is reached, and how much leadership that takes is its own decision.

Officers cannot be set above 110, which is an engine limit. Diplomacy takes influences already running into account. Leadership is handed out to officers first, then spies, then diplomacy, and research takes whatever is left.
with the slider AI on, the game stops automatically continuing research once a level finishes.
No country selected - pages fall back to the actual player.
Any country's tag, whether anyone is playing it or not.
Press Get players to scan. In single player this lists only you.
A player can block the host from selecting their country. The selection silently stays put in that case.
Hiding a decision only takes it out of your own decision list. The AI carries on using it either way, so this is about a tidy list rather than about how the game plays.
Each run writes to its own folder, so a new game does not overwrite the last one. Assigned on the first collection.
Assigned when collection first writes something.
Meant for development: collection writes a file per statistic per country every day, which the game feels. Restricting it to a few countries keeps that in hand.
Every human player is collected while the switch above is off. The list is still editable.
Statistics appear here once collection has been switched on for a while. Each day writes one line per statistic.
Nothing to plot: the files ticked hold no readings.
The file carries on past a crash or a reload from an earlier save. Readings from the timeline that was abandoned are dropped rather than plotted alongside the one that replaced it.
Click it, then press the key to use. Escape cancels. A letter still types normally into a text box, so only a key pressed outside one opens the window.
Puts the window back where and as large as it first stood
Dark grey panels with a blue accent. Easiest to pick out over a busy map.
Paper: the window as a document over the map. For playing in daylight, or if the dark style is hard to read.
Dark blue panels, the drawing library's first look.
Scrolling the map at the screen edge, where event popups appear and the two custom autosaves are in the game's own Options window on OpenHOI3, on its Game tab.
Reads the mod's modifier files, which takes a moment.
What each national focus gives once it has been active long enough. A tier includes everything from the tiers before it only where the mod repeats it, so read each column on its own.
